page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7.4xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 8 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8369B processor running at 2.7 GHz. The instance is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 2.0 GB per core ratio. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying instead on network-attached storage and featuring a baseline network bandwidth of 10 Gbps.

The x86_64 architecture of the Intel Xeon processor includes advanced instruction sets such as AVX, AVX-512F, and AVX-512_VNNI, which accelerate vector calculations and machine learning inference. It also supports cryptographic acceleration via AES, VAES, and SHA_NI, alongside bit manipulation extensions like BMI2 and FMA. The CPU cache configuration consists of 48 KB L1 data cache, 1 MB L2 cache, and 48 MB L3 cache.

Benchmark evaluations place the ecs.c7.4xlarge consistently in the average performance tier. The instance achieved a single-core stress-ng score of 1846.58 and a multi-core score of 15477.28. Memory bandwidth tests show 847.6 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 93.71 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. In application-specific workloads, it processed 15.34 million Redis SET operations per second and delivered a static web serving throughput of 18.93 GB/sec. However, a performance tradeoff is observed in LLM inference tasks; while it handles a small 135M model at 1281.68 tokens/sec for prompt processing, its performance drops to a weak rating of 31.09 tokens/sec when processing prompts for a medium 7B model.

Given its compute-focused hardware profile and dedicated CPU allocation, the instance offers balanced cost efficiency for workloads requiring sustained CPU performance without massive memory footprints. It is well-suited for tasks such as software compilation, web serving, database operations, and moderate text or image processing.
